title: Nowcasting using regression on signatures: the continuous time Kalman--Bucy filter as a linear function of the signature
author: Samuel N. Cohen, Giulia Mantoan, Lars Nesheim, \'Aureo de Paula, Arthur Turrell, Lingyi Yang
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem (source0.tex lines 371--373, source label thm:KalmanRepresentation): the continuous time Kalman--Bucy filter, including the case of deterministic time-varying parameters, is a linear function of its initial estimate and of the signature of the time-augmented observation process, and only signature terms in which the observation appears once are needed; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 376--405 (one adjacent proof environment of 30 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span. It rewrites the filter through the natural time-varying change of notation, introduces the iterated integrals of the drift matrix and of the driving term, observes that both solve the same recurrence and are super-polynomially small so that the two infinite series converge, writes the filter in integral form, exhibits the explicit series solution and verifies it against the integral equation, and then shows that each iterated integral is a linear function of the signature of the time-augmented path: the deterministic time-dependent coefficients are expanded through the signature of time using the Stone--Weierstrass approximation and the elementary form of the signature of time, and the stochastic term is handled by a mean-square polynomial approximation when the coefficient matrix is not continuous, with that case treated in a footnote inside the proof. The argument is an original representation theorem of the article's Section 3 (the paper's central theoretical claim, announced as "signatures generalise linear Kalman filters"), and it is the result on which the article's nowcasting methodology rests. H2: a research-level representation theorem of rough-path and filtering theory whose complete proof combines Picard-series convergence, iterated-integral recurrences, Stone--Weierstrass density of polynomials in time and a mean-square density argument, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
